Programme Overview

Join the International Max Planck Research School for Molecular Organ Biology (IMPRS-MOB) and unlock a world of opportunities as a fully funded PhD candidate. Our innovative graduate program IMPRS-MOB is set in the vibrant Rhine-Main region, connecting three leading scientific hubs: MPI for Heart and Lung Research in Bad Nauheim, Justus Liebig University in Gießen, and Goethe University Frankfurt.

Fields of Research

  • Genetics
  • Development
  • Regeneration
  • Stem Cell Biology
  • Cancer
  • Cardiopulmonary Research

Eligibility

Applicants should hold an MSc with a strong background in biological sciences, biochemistry, medicine, pharmacy or a related discipline by October 2026.

What We Offer

  • An international and structured PhD program taught in English
  • Excellent career opportunities and working conditions
  • State-of-the-art facilities and research projects
  • Feedback, guidance and mentorship by an individual Thesis Advisory Committee
  • Fully funded PhD position

About IMPRS for Molecular Organ Biology

The International Max Planck Research School for Molecular Organ Biology provides doctoral training in Germany at the intersection of molecular biology and organ research. IMPRS-MOB brings together partner research institutions and universities. Doctoral researchers investigate biological mechanisms through supervised projects, scientific training and collaboration within an international life sciences community.

Official website: https://imprs-mob.mpg.de

Important Notes

  • Applications only through online application platform.

  • Fully funded PhD positions for three years.

Contact

Questions about this position, eligibility or the application process should be raised through the contact channel given on the official announcement page (see the Official Link section above). Always quote the position reference in your message so the admissions or HR team can route your enquiry quickly.

How to Apply

Submit your application through the official portal before the deadline: 11 November 2026. Read the eligibility requirements carefully and prepare all requested documents — early applications are strongly recommended for competitive awards.
